get.description:
Title, texts, documentation link, severity and group of every health and security check, ordered by type, DBMS family and display order. The texts describe the check itself and are the same for every user and server. A server's results already include them: see `GET /v1/servers/{id}/health-checks` and `GET /v1/servers/{id}/security-checks`, whose check names match `key`.

The same `key` can appear once per DBMS family with different texts, so match on `type`, `dbms` and `key` together.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Return only checks of this type. Omit for both.

parameters.name: dbms
parameters.description: Return only checks of this DBMS family. `mysql` covers MySQL and MariaDB. Omit for both.

422.description: `type` or `dbms` is not one of the allowed values.

changes.before: The current state of the newest configuration of each server the authenticated user owns, ordered by server. A server without configurations is omitted.
changes.after: The current configuration state of each server the authenticated user owns, ordered by server: the newest state of the server, whichever configuration it belongs to. A server without configuration states is omitted.

changes.before: List Latest Configurations for All User Servers
changes.after: List Current Configurations for All User Servers

changes.before: Every configuration state of one server, applied or not, newest first — the list Releem Platform shows. Each row is one state of a configuration, so a configuration that was applied or rolled back appears once per state; `configuration_id` groups them. All states are returned unless `limit` is given. With `latest=true` only the current state of the newest configuration is returned, or an empty list when the server has none.
changes.after: Every configuration state of one server, applied or not, newest first — the list Releem Platform shows. Each row is one state of a configuration, so a configuration that was applied or rolled back appears once per state; `configuration_id` groups them. All states are returned unless `limit` is given. With `latest=true` only the server's current state is returned — its newest state, the first row of the full list — or an empty list when the server has none.

changes.before:
Server metadata with the health and security checks that currently fail. Every check, passing or failing, with its value: `GET /v1/servers/{id}/health-checks` and `GET /v1/servers/{id}/security-checks`.

Recognized security findings remain available when part of a report cannot be interpreted. Unresolved entries are returned in security_checks_unknown, and security_checks_decode_error describes any interpretation error. An empty security_checks object does not establish that all checks passed: inspect these fields and use the security-checks endpoint for the complete report. When no report is available, security_checks is empty and security_checks_decode_error is null.
changes.after:
Server metadata with every health and security check of the latest report, passing or failing, in display order. Each check carries its result and its catalog texts: title, descriptions, documentation link, severity and group.

Recognized security findings remain available when part of a report cannot be interpreted. Unresolved entries are returned in security_checks_unknown, and security_checks_decode_error describes any interpretation error. An empty security_checks object does not establish that all checks passed: inspect these fields. When no report is available, security_checks is empty and security_checks_decode_error is null.

changes.before: Every health check of the server's latest report, with its value.
changes.after: Every health check of the server's latest report, in display order, with its result, value and catalog texts: title, descriptions, documentation link and group. MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL servers have different checks. A check the catalog has no entry for is listed last with null texts.

changes.before: Average, minimum and maximum of every metric of one server over a window, computed from hourly trends in one read. A metric without trend data in the window is listed with null values. `start_time` and `end_time` are required; a reversed range is rejected with 400 `invalid_time_range` and a window longer than 366 days with 400 `time_range_too_wide`. Request two windows to compare a period with the previous one.
changes.after: Average, minimum and maximum of every metric of one server over a window, computed from hourly trends in one read. A metric without trend data in the window is listed with null values. `start_time` and `end_time` are required; a reversed range is rejected with 400 `invalid_time_range` and a window longer than 366 days with 400 `time_range_too_wide`. The window includes `start_time` and excludes `end_time`, so adjacent windows do not overlap; request two windows to compare a period with the previous one. Values that are not finite numbers are returned as null.

changes.before: Retrieve query execution statistics for a time window. The window is `[start_date, start_date + period_days)`, or the last `period_days` up to now without `start_date`. Percentages are relative to every query that passes the filters, so with `schema_name` they are shares of that schema.
changes.after: Retrieve query execution statistics for a time window. The window is `[start_date, start_date + period)`, `[start_date, end_date)`, or the last `period` up to now without `start_date`. The start is included and the end is excluded in every mode. An explicit `end_date` requires `start_date` and overrides `period`; it must be later than the start. Bounds use second precision. Percentages are relative to every query that passes the filters, so with `schema_name` they are shares of that schema. The period is a positive integer optionally followed by `m` (minutes), `h` (hours), or `d` (days); a bare integer means days. Other suffixes are rejected.

changes.before: Every security check of the server's latest security snapshot, with its value. Check names follow the snapshot's engine: MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL use separate catalogs. Account checks can fail with a null value when the producer did not include account details. Unsupported failure codes or mixed/ambiguous engine fields return `422 invalid_source_data`; they are not returned as an empty successful snapshot.
changes.after: Every security check of the server's latest security snapshot, in display order, with its result, value and catalog texts: title, descriptions, documentation link, severity and group. A check the catalog has no entry for is listed last with null texts. Check names follow the snapshot's engine: MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL use separate catalogs. Account checks can fail with a null value when the producer did not include account details. Unsupported failure codes or mixed/ambiguous engine fields return `422 invalid_source_data`; they are not returned as an empty successful snapshot.

before.name: Server Writes
before.description: Writes for one server. Like the reads, every route requires the authenticated user to own the server named by `{id}` (canonical decimal form). Every write that passes body validation is recorded in the API audit log, including ones refused by the ownership or record checks. New tasks and query optimization records use the request processing time as their status timestamp. Updating a query optimization record does not change its status timestamp.

before.name: Server Diagnostics
before.description: Server-scoped read endpoints for one server's details, configuration history, query optimizations, metrics, deadlocks, agent tasks, processlist captures, and schema checks. All routes require the authenticated user to own the server named by `{id}`; an unknown or foreign server ID returns 404. `{id}` must be the canonical decimal form — `00101` or `abc` returns 404 on every route rather than being cast to a number.
